name: Beeswax
aliases: E901, INS 901, beeswax, bee wax, white beeswax, yellow beeswax, white wax, yellow wax
what_is: A wax produced by honeybees and used on the surface of foods as a glazing and protective coating.
why_botia: Beeswax coats the surface of foods to give them shine and protect them — it is what makes apples and gummies gleam. It is barely digested and passes through the body almost intact. Its animal origin matters to people who eat vegan, and on fresh fruit it does not appear in an ingredient list because the fruit does not carry one.
can_1: Identify E901, INS 901, beeswax and common white or yellow beeswax declarations.
can_2: Explain that it is a bee-derived glazing coating and show the animal-origin, texture and E-number layers.
cannot_1: Determine how much beeswax is present or how thick the coating is from a standard ingredient list.
cannot_2: Determine from an unlabelled piece of fresh fruit whether beeswax or another glazing treatment was used.

sources.label: EU Regulation 1333/2008 — E901 beeswax uses as glazing agent
EU Regulation 1169/2011 — foods exempt from a mandatory ingredients list

title: Beeswax
description: Beeswax (E901) is a bee-derived glazing wax used to give foods shine and protection; it is barely digested and can matter for vegan choices.
